lines: Build your own ride, one set at a time.
Pick Intervals. Every set, the warm-up and the cool-down has its own times, levels and cadence aim.
It starts with Descending recoveries: a five-minute warm-up, then five sets of thirty-second efforts at level twenty-eight.
The recoveries shrink from three minutes to none, then a cool-down.
The preview adds it up: thirty minutes.
Edit opens a dialog. Give set two a third round, and save.
The row and the total follow: thirty-three minutes.
The warm-up and the cool-down have their own dialog, and a switch to leave them out.
Add set copies the last one. Move a set up or down, or remove it.
Or start from Even sets: three sets of four efforts, seventeen minutes in all.
On a phone, every row keeps its actions within reach.
What the tests prove: a plan holds at most thirty efforts and a hundred and eighty minutes.
And the last Intervals plan you started comes back after a reload.
That is journey five. Wattzup turns an Echelon bike into a live training display.
